name: Louisiana Tech University
old_description: Step into one of the fastest-growing and highest-paying fields with Louisiana Tech’s Graduate Certificate in Data Science. With a booming job market — over 650% growth since 2012 and millions of new roles projected by 2026 — data science offers unparalleled career opportunities. This certificate program equips you with practical skills to access, manage, manipulate, and transform data using the latest programming techniques and popular data visualization tools.
about:
Louisiana Tech University was founded on July 6, 1894, in Ruston, Louisiana, as a public institution. It began as a regional college and has grown into a comprehensive university serving north-central Louisiana.

The university offers more than 135 degree and certificate programs across undergraduate, graduate, and professional levels. It operates on a quarter system, with a total enrollment of 12,039 students and a student-faculty ratio of 21:1. The campus centers on a pedestrian-friendly quad in Ruston, a town of approximately 22,000 residents.

Louisiana Tech serves students preparing for careers in engineering, business, health sciences, liberal arts, and applied sciences. The school partners with employers such as Big Four accounting firms and regional industry for internships, co-ops, and workforce development initiatives.

The university emphasizes hands-on learning and real-world applications, particularly in its engineering programs. Over 90% of students receive some form of financial assistance, and the institution's mission prioritizes teaching, research, creative activity, public service, and economic development.

name: Loving West Virginia
old_description: Unleash mythical creatures with Cryptid Playing Cards. Each deck features iconic cryptids like Mothman, Bigfoot, Flatwoods Monster, and Batboy perfect for any card game. Embrace the unknown and add some mystery to your next game night.
about:
Loving West Virginia operates from Fairmont, West Virginia, selling state-themed merchandise through its e-commerce site lovingwv.com. The founding year, ownership structure, and founders are not disclosed in the available sources.

The company curates and sells a range of West Virginia–branded products including Cryptid Playing Cards featuring Mothman, Bigfoot, Flatwoods Monster, and Batboy; apparel such as unisex and youth shirts; stickers and vinyl decals; 8×10 art prints on 100 lb cardstock; a West Virginia scratch map covering all 55 counties; glassware, can coolers, and holiday ornaments. It also runs a monthly mystery sticker subscription club. No manufacturing processes, facility size, headcount, or production volumes are described.

Customers are individual consumers seeking West Virginia souvenirs, gifts, and novelty items. The product line references local landmarks (Barrackville Bridge, New River), state symbols (304 area code, state buck), and regional folklore (Mothman, Flatwoods Monster). No industrial, OEM, or B2B customer segments are mentioned.

The company emphasizes designs that celebrate West Virginia culture, folklore, and geography, and it directs a portion of certain sales to flood relief and children's hospital fundraisers. No explicit statement about competitive differentiation or founding mission is provided beyond the product themes.

about:
Lumen Food Labs LLC, operating as Lumen Brands, is based in Chicago, Illinois, and was founded in 2020. The company maintains its headquarters and warehouse in the city. Ownership details and founder names are not publicly disclosed.

The firm provides master distributor services, Foreign Supplier Verification Program (FSVP) and Qualified Importer (QI) compliance, and FDA-registered third-party logistics (3PL) warehousing and fulfillment designed for consumer packaged goods. It also offers monthly accounting, sales reporting, and forecasting, and acts as Importer of Record, customs broker, clearing house, insurer, and FDA Responsible Party for inbound shipments. The company purchases inventory upfront at wholesale pricing.

Lumen serves consumer packaged goods brands, particularly food and beverage companies seeking to enter the U.S. market. Its brand partners are typically foreign suppliers that require end-to-end compliance, distribution, and regulatory support to sell into the United States.

The company states that it aligns its incentives with partners by only profiting when products sell, matching investment dollar-for-dollar, and purchasing inventory upfront to reduce risk for suppliers.

name: Luray Textiles Inc. - Plant (NOT the store)
old_description: LuRay Textiles, Inc. is a manufacturer of knitted fabrics. We use American made yarn in the production of our cloth. We offer a variety of fabrics from cotton and polyester to Kevlar®, Nomex® and PBI®.
about:
LuRay Textiles, Inc. operates a knitted-fabric mill in North Wilkesboro, North Carolina. The company was founded in 1984 and has remained a domestic producer of technical and commodity textiles.

The mill produces knitted fabrics using American-sourced yarn, running fibers that range from cotton and polyester to high-performance aramids such as Kevlar®, Nomex® and PBI®. In addition to yard goods, the facility manufactures wiping cloths and rags cut for automotive detailing, furniture finishing and general industrial cleaning.

Customers span apparel brands, safety-gear manufacturers, automotive aftermarket suppliers and woodworking shops. The fabric line is sold in multiple weights and widths for garments, protective sleeves and other sewn products, while the wiping-cloth assortment targets car-care retailers and furniture refinishers.

LuRay emphasizes its U.S.-based supply chain, stating that all yarn is American-made and that production is carried out by a domestic workforce. The company positions this origin as a differentiator for buyers seeking traceable, Berry-compliant textiles.

name: M-Tron Components Inc
old_description: Since 1984, M-TRON Components has maintained a commitment to excellence and has provided our customers with a secure supply chain
about:
M-Tron Components Inc. is based in Ronkonkoma, New York. Founded in 1984, the company is a veteran-owned small business that began as a supplier of electronic components for military and commercial markets.

The company operates as a franchised distributor, stocking a broad inventory of semiconductors, resistors, capacitors, interconnect devices, and computer products from authorized manufacturers. It also provides value-added services including Mil‑Spec packaging per MIL‑STD‑2073, printed circuit board assembly, kitting, and tape‑and‑reel packaging. An exclusive “Search and Sell Network” helps customers source obsolete or allocated parts.

M-Tron serves the military, aerospace, and commercial sectors, supplying the U.S. Government and its subcontractors as well as OEMs in defense and industrial applications. Its customer base includes prime contractors and end‑users requiring traceable, counterfeit‑free components.

The business emphasizes a secure supply chain, holding ISO 9001:2015 and AS9120:2016 certifications, NDAA compliance, and H.R.‑1540 certification. Its counterfeit‑free zone and franchised distributor status are presented as key differentiators.

name: M.S. Fabrication
old_description: M.S. Fabrication, located in Dorchester, MA, offers custom sheet metal fabrication services. There is no project we can’t handle. Our experienced team of metalworkers can flawlessly execute even the most complex designs. We operate in a large warehouse, filled with a massive selection of state-of-the-art machines designed to handle pretty much anything.
about:
M.S. Fabrication operates from a warehouse in Dorchester Center, Massachusetts, just south of downtown Boston. The shop specializes in custom sheet metal fabrication, serving clients with a range of forming, cutting, and welding capabilities.

The facility houses a broad inventory of equipment, including two press brakes—a 12-foot, 250-ton Accurpress and a 10-foot, 140-ton Trumpf V-130 with six-axis control—along with a 60-inch pyramid roll, a Buffalo angle and tube rolling machine, a 10-foot Accurshear hydraulic shear, a 60-by-120-inch Omax CNC waterjet capable of cutting up to six inches thick, and a Euromax BX 1000 ironworker. Welding stations feature a Miller Dynasty 350 TIG, a Miller Matic 250 MIG, a 20-inch throat spot welder, and a 1,200-watt fiber laser welder. The company works with common steel, stainless steel, and aluminum alloys.

M.S. Fabrication accepts custom projects from clients requiring sheet metal work, though it does not publicly list specific industry verticals or named customers.

name: MADE Apparel Services
old_description: Founded in 2020, MADE helps creators move sewn-product ideas toward production with clarity and confidence. Whether you’re refining a first concept, improving an existing design, or strengthening a home-studio workflow, we take a structured, transparent approach that supports consistent quality and informed decision-making.
about:
MADE Apparel Services was founded in 2020 by Heather Zager in Renton, Washington. Zager’s path to founding the company began with a patternmaking course in 2014, followed by an Associate of Applied Science in Apparel Design and Development from Seattle Central College. She spent two years at Meta integrating electronics and haptic components into wearable sewn products, and now teaches patternmaking and fit at her alma mater while also developing her own patent‑pending product, Zcissors.

The consultancy delivers end‑to‑end product development for sewn goods: pattern development using CLO3D and Alvanon digital forms, sewn prototyping with production‑intent construction, pattern grading via industry‑standard CAD tools, and comprehensive tech packs that organize bills of materials, construction sequences, and stitch specifications. A two‑person team — Zager and administrative support Nirosha Rodrigo — operates from a Seattle‑area base, guiding clients through each stage with a structured, transparent workflow.

Clients range from early‑stage startups to established brands and corporate teams. Projects have spanned equestrian apparel (Whinny Equestrian), postpartum recovery garments (Luna Azzurra Care), sustainable womenswear (Springtime & Harvest), supportive sports bras (Wrax), and functional accessories such as the Book Carrier Bookmark. The firm also draws on Zager’s wearable‑technology background to support soft‑goods concepts that incorporate sensors or electronics.

Zager started MADE to give creators a clear, organized path from concept to manufacture, emphasizing collaboration, respect, and inclusivity. The company’s differentiator is its focus on delivering production‑ready documentation alongside the practical knowledge clients need to make confident decisions as they scale.

about:
MAGNA Pharmaceuticals, Inc. was founded on August 1, 1990, in Louisville, Kentucky, as a family-owned United States pharmaceutical company. Dr. Warren P. Lesser serves as president and chief executive officer, guiding the business with a stated commitment to accountability and community responsibility.

The company develops and manufactures pharmaceutical products and dietary supplements, with a focus on unique, non-substitutable formulations. Its flagship product, Stahist T, contains the antihistamine triprolidine and is formulated as scored tablets to allow half-tablet dosing for customized patient therapy. All products are produced to high quality standards, though the company does not disclose facility size, headcount, or annual production volumes.

MAGNA serves the healthcare sector, supplying products to patients, clinicians, and institutional buyers. The firm maintains memberships in the Wound, Ostomy, and Continence Nurses Society and the Specialty Pharma Association, indicating engagement with wound-care, ostomy, and continence nursing specialties as well as the broader specialty pharmaceutical market.

The company’s stated mission is to provide non-substitutable products and services at reasonable prices with genuine concern for stakeholders. Dr. Lesser has emphasized that the business exists to help people rather than solely to generate profit, a philosophy reflected in the “accountability” tagline incorporated into the corporate logo.

name: MCT Industries Inc.
old_description: MCT specializes in providing installation, parts and service for truck bodies, trailers, refuse and water equipment, roll-off and trash containers, snow removal equipment, road construction equipment and custom fabrication to outfit your purchase to your exact specifications. MCT stocks over 10,000 parts for over 200 types of equipment and trailers. We strive to provide high quality parts and service to our customers. Have a hard to find part? We've got over 40 years in the business and our parts team is well seasoned in the industry to help you identify and locate those hard to find parts.
about:
MCT Industries Inc. was founded in 1974 in Albuquerque, New Mexico, as a family-owned and operated business. The company began with trailer sales and repairs and has since expanded into a full-service provider for truck bodies, trailers, and heavy equipment.

Today, MCT operates a custom fabrication facility equipped with a plasma cutter, laser cutter, 20-foot press brake, and shear. The company installs and customizes flatbeds, service bodies, dump bodies, and crane bodies, and provides hydraulic system service, refuse vehicle maintenance, DOT inspections, and snow-removal equipment installation such as salt spreaders and plows. It also supplies wetline kits, combo kits, walking-floor systems, end-dump trailers, and spray kits for herbicide and water trucks. A government manufacturing division handles design, prototype development, and full-rate production of items including nuclear and chemical munitions transporters, self-propelled ground support equipment, and large-scale plant fabrication. The parts department stocks more than 10,000 components for over 200 equipment types, and the company offers equipment rentals and roll-off waste services.

MCT serves state, city, and county agencies and municipalities, holding several State and CES contracts. Its government division works with military and federal customers, while its commercial division supports fleets, heavy-equipment operators, and construction contractors. The waste division provides roll-off service in the Albuquerque area and residential service in Santa Fe.

The company emphasizes its four-decade track record and a parts team experienced in locating hard-to-find components. Its government manufacturing plant highlights a capability to take projects from concept through full-rate production, a differentiator noted in its own materials.

name: MEI Electrical Contractors & Systems Integrators
old_description: MEI Electrical Contractors & Systems Integrators is a versatile full-service electrical contracting company with a 25-year proven track record of providing premier electrical, fire alarm, and security system design, installation, maintenance, testing, inspection, repair, and monitoring for commercial, industrial, educational, governmental, health care, agricultural, and residential applications throughout Vermont and New Hampshire.
about:
MEI Electrical Contractors & Systems Integrators is based in Westfield, Vermont. The company traces its roots to 1991 when it was founded as Mike’s Electric, Inc. in Jay, Vermont. A branch office opened in Williston in 2013 to serve Chittenden County and western Vermont. The fire alarm and security divisions were spun off as MEI Systems Integrators in 2014. In 2017, then‑President Adam Fortier acquired the business and relocated it to a larger facility in Westfield.

Today MEI provides full‑service electrical contracting along with fire alarm and security system design, installation, maintenance, testing, inspection, repair, and monitoring. The firm employs over 65 people, including master and journeyman electricians, certified fire alarm and security technicians, project managers, designers, and estimators. Its capabilities span design/build projects, lighting design and conservation, electrical service upgrades, 24‑hour emergency response, network infrastructure, access control, video surveillance, and fiber optics. Project experience ranges from residential generator installations to multi‑million‑dollar commercial and industrial new construction, including solar and renewable energy work.

MEI serves commercial, industrial, health care, educational, agricultural, governmental (federal, state, and local), and residential customers throughout Vermont and New Hampshire, with government contracts extending into New York, Maine, and Massachusetts. Long‑standing general‑contractor partners include DEW Construction Corp., PeakCM LLC, Bread Loaf Corporation, ReArch Company, Wright & Morrissey Inc., and Kingsbury Companies.

The company emphasizes a “Site Management Strategy” to coordinate schedules, priorities, and participants for turn‑key delivery, and it operates a Customer Alarm Portal for system monitoring. MEI participates in the Vermont Registered Apprenticeship program to train new electricians and highlights its safety record and continuous training. Its stated mission is to provide efficient, quality work on time and on budget while fostering a family‑focused workplace with advancement opportunities.
